concerns.text: The plan states that outliers will be detected relative to the semicircle bulk edge (±2), but the research document (research.md) defines outlier detection using an *empirical* bulk edge estimated as the 99th percentile of the spectrum. This creates a construct‑validity mismatch and a circularity risk: the bulk edge is derived from the same data used to flag outliers, potentially biasing outlier counts, especially for small perturbations.

Only 100 repetitions per configuration are planned, giving a maximum standard error of ≈0.05 for outlier probabilities. This sample size may be insufficient to locate the critical threshold θ_c with the precision needed to claim verification of the BBP transition; confidence intervals could be too wide to distinguish the theoretical θ≈1 from nearby values.

Matrix dimension N is varied up to 2000, yet the plan does not include a systematic control or analysis of N as a potential confound. Since finite‑size effects can shift the apparent bulk edge and eigenvalue fluctuations, results may conflate the impact of N with that of θ, k, or sparsity density p.

The plan states that outliers will be detected “relative to the semicircle bulk edge (±2)”, but the research description (research.md:~45) defines the bulk edge empirically as the 99th percentile of the same eigenvalue sample and then flags outliers as λ > bulk_edge + 0.05. Using the data‑derived bulk edge to both define the outlier threshold and evaluate outlier occurrence creates a circular validation: the outcome (outlier count) is directly dependent on a statistic computed from the same outcome, biasing the estimated critical θ_c.
